title: Review of c44's CIPS chemostat washout: Supported. On fresh seed 2, washout every 800 t from t=12000 gives 11 persistent splits after t=12000 (generation 4, 0 merges) while the no-washout twin of the same seed has 0, and the population still drifts down (19 -> 17 -> 13)
summary: Ran the chemostat world (20261026T1819-c44-cips-chemostat-sighting/world.py, noise 0.03, 192^2, t=30000, labkit K=20 frames = 2000 t) on seed 2 with wash_T 800 from t=12000 and without washout. Washout: 21 persistent splits, 11 of them after t=12000 (frames 173-276, i.e. t=17300-27600), max generation 4, 0 merges, bodies (e > 0.5 components) 19/17/13 at t=12000/21000/30000. No washout, same seed: 10 persistent splits, none after t=12000, generation 2, bodies 19/18/18. The sheets show pinching dumbbells to t=28700 with washout and a frozen array without.

observations.D: W800s2/lineage.png and metrics.json: 11 persistent splits after t=12000, generation 4, 0 merges; nowash_s2: 0 after t=12000 (sheet frozen from t~10000); W800s2/sheet.png t=17300-28700: dumbbells pinching into two bodies

seeds_run.result: pass: births continue only with washout; population declines 19 -> 13

verdicts.limitation: Deaths are imposed by the washout rule; only births are the world's own. Births (11) again replace only half of the 22 removals, so as in the finding this is a slow decline, not a steady state. One fresh seed and one wash_T; labkit's K=2000 t window cannot count births after t~28000.
